Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated (noisy neighbor / SLOs)

Hi Sofia / Carlos —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through FinPay's use case. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can scope recommendations: 

Key points we heard on the call:
- Expected traffic: ~10k API calls/day with spiky traffic (peaks up to ~200 req/s during settlement windows)
- Latency targets: p95 generation latency target ~200ms for customer-facing flows; lower for internal batch jobs
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 scope, strict audit logs, and data isolation for PII-heavy requests
- Preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable performance, but want to understand the cost delta vs Hosted API and whether Private VPC is required for regulatory reasons
- Primary concerns: "noisy neighbor" behavior on shared pools, guaranteed isolation boundaries, and measurable SLOs for latency & availability

What I can do next:
1) Share Redwood's SOC 2 summary and our Dedicated product brief (attached).
2) Schedule a short infra deep-dive with our Dedicated product/infra lead (Priyom) to go over isolation model, SLA guarantees, and noisy-neighbor mitigation strategies. We'll cover what we benchmark, how we enforce isolation, and what configuration options (e.g., pinning, reserved pools) are available.
3) Provide a rough cost range for Dedicated reserved capacity vs Hosted API based on your traffic profile after the deep-dive.

Proposed times for the infra deep-dive: Friday Jul 17 at 11:00 AM PT or Monday Jul 20 at 10:00 AM PT — please let me know which works. If you can share any additional traffic history or non-functional requirements (throughput / retention / encryption at rest keys), that will help us prepare.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf, redwood-dedicated-brief.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Best,

From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated (noisy neighbor / SLOs)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap and the materials. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Preference: We are currently leaning toward Dedicated capacity because predictable latency during settlement spikes is a high priority. We want to avoid tail latency caused by noisy neighbors in a shared pool.
- Traffic profile: Average ~8k API calls/day; peak windows toward end of day can hit ~300 req/s for short bursts (1-3 minutes). Monthly token volume is ~120M tokens.
- SLOs: We need p95 latency <= 200ms for customer-facing calls and 99.95% availability. We also need KV/prefix caching to be preserved across requests for session-based flows.
- Security: SOC 2 is mandatory; we also need audit logs for all calls and support for customer-managed keys (KMS) if possible.

Questions we want covered in the infra deep-dive:
1) For Dedicated: What isolation guarantees do you provide? Are workloads single-tenant on GPUs or multi-tenant within the pool? How do you handle resource contention?
2) For Hosted API: What noisy-neighbor mitigations exist (priority queues, request shaping)? Can you provide benchmark results for latency p95/p99 under mixed workloads?
3) For Private VPC: What additional network/data controls exist and how long does onboarding typically take?

We can do Jul 17 at 11:00 AM PT — that works for our infra lead (Carlos) and me. Also, please include a high-level cost range for Dedicated vs Hosted so we can compare internally.

On the attachments: I reviewed the SOC2 summary — looks good, but we'll also include Redwood in our vendor security questionnaire in parallel.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramirez
Director of Engineering, FinPay
sofia@finpay.com
